title: Strong randomized recognition implies randomized recognition
statement: Let $E$ be a verifier model, let $L$ be a language of bit strings, and let $d$ be a natural number. If there is an efficient verifier with a polynomial random-bit bound that rejects every nonmember for every choice of random bits and accepts each member $x$ with probability at least $1-(1/2)^{(|x|+1)^d+1}$, then $L$ has an efficient verifier with a polynomial random-bit bound that accepts every member with probability at least $2/3$ and rejects every nonmember for every choice of random bits.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language of bit strings
$L$ has an efficient verifier with polynomially many random bits, the stated member acceptance probability, and certain rejection on nonmembers
